It builds a new dict and increments the count for `record['timestamp'][:10]`, the UTC date of the loader's normalized timestamp. Empty input gives `{}`.\n\nThe function does not mutate its input. Its result is a plain dict of integers, so it is JSON-serializable.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nThe `daily` module was a stub. `python3 -m logreports input.jsonl --report daily` now prints per-date counts as JSON with sorted keys. The CLI already calls `summarize(records)`, so no CLI change was needed.\n\n## Files\n\n- `logreports/reports/daily.py`: the implementation.\n- `tests/test_daily.py`: unittest cases for empty input, single record, same-day aggregation, multiple dates, the UTC midnight boundary, fractional seconds, non-mutation, JSON serializability, and the CLI with populated, empty and offset (`-02:00`) input.\n- `docs/reports/daily.md`: output shape, the UTC date rule, empty behavior, and CLI usage.\n- `app_docs/daily.md`: this record.\n\n`logreports/core.py` and `logreports/__main__.py` are unchanged.\n\n## How to verify\n\n```\npython3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests\npython3 -m logreports input.jsonl --report daily\n```\n\nThe controller's `test` and `build` checks and the independent review decide acceptance.
